propositions: The outbound mapper injects _assignee_resolver as an attribute using try/except that silently fails if injection cannot occur, causing permanent non-authoritative assignee resolution and infinite re-emission churn.

The attribute injection is invisible to the type checker and allowed dead-code patterns (PR #120 Data Center adapter's entire authoritative branch was unreachable because the attribute was never set).

The resolver dependency is undeclared in the OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee contract, forcing consumers to discover it via getattr with a non-authoritative fallback instead of enforcing presence at call sites.

Threading the resolver from compute_update_fields through diff_canonical_fields to resolve_assignee requires an intermediate parameter hop that does not exist in the current attribute-injection design.

DC's constructor-bound resolver and the core's per-jira_key resolver have different lifecycles; the core must overwrite the constructor one, and this semantic must be preserved as an explicit preference order.
